raw_response:
I am getting old now, so I do not like to change too much. On my 2 mu, I will still do wheat and then maize after wheat, same as before. This is the safest way for my family. Wheat gives us steady grain, and maize after that brings the second harvest. I only finished primary school, so I do not calculate like the technicians do. I look at what happened in my own field and what the neighbors are doing. Last years when I cut fertilizer too much, the wheat was thin and yellow, so this year I will not save on that too much. But money is still tight because some family members work outside and cash must be kept for daily life, so I will use a middle amount, not the highest.

For wheat, I will sow in early October with the local common improved seed people nearby buy from the dealer. I will put base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress once when the wheat starts growing fast in spring. Since we have well water, I will irrigate a few times for wheat because wheat here really depends on water. After wheat harvest in June, I will rush to plant summer maize right away, with little delay. The maize window is short, so I will keep tillage simple and use the same practical method as most people here. For maize I will also use a moderate fertilizer rate and usually irrigate once or twice depending on rain. If insects or weeds show up, I will spray, but I do not like wasting money on too many chemicals unless I see a problem.
